label: Formulated the Impartial Spectator as the foundation of conscience and objective moral judgment
description: Adam Smith formulated and introduced the concept of "The Impartial Spectator", which became a seminal contribution in ethics philosophy.
dialecticalTension: Formulating an epistemic apparatus to resolve central problems in ethics.
historicalContext: Introduced during the Enlightenment & Social Contract as part of Adam Smith's canonical writings.

label: Systematized the division of labor as the primary catalyst of productivity and national wealth
description: Adam Smith formulated and introduced the concept of "Division of Labor", which became a seminal contribution in political philosophy.
dialecticalTension: Formulating an epistemic apparatus to resolve central problems in political.
historicalContext: Introduced during the Enlightenment & Social Contract as part of Adam Smith's canonical writings.

label: Introduced the invisible hand to theorize spontaneous market order and decentralized resource coordination
description: Adam Smith formulated and introduced the concept of "The Invisible Hand", which became a seminal contribution in political philosophy.
dialecticalTension: Formulating an epistemic apparatus to resolve central problems in political.
historicalContext: Introduced during the Enlightenment & Social Contract as part of Adam Smith's canonical writings.

label: Smith's Theory of Moral Sentiments and impartial spectator directly influenced Kant's moral philosophy and formulations of conscience
description: Immanuel Kant was fundamentally influenced by Adam Smith's central inquiries, which shaped the evolution of their philosophical worldview.
dialecticalTension: Negotiating the intellectual shift from Adam Smith's perspective to Immanuel Kant's reconstructed system.
historicalContext: Inter-epochal reception: transmitting insights from the Enlightenment & Social Contract across history into the German Idealism & Romanticism.

label: Hegel drew upon Smith's political economy to construct his concept of civil society (bürgerliche Gesellschaft) and the system of needs
description: G.W.F. Hegel adopted Adam Smith's insights and systematically extended them into new metaphysical, ethical, or epistemological domains.
dialecticalTension: Negotiating the intellectual shift from Adam Smith's perspective to G.W.F. Hegel's reconstructed system.
historicalContext: Inter-epochal reception: transmitting insights from the Enlightenment & Social Contract across history into the German Idealism & Romanticism.

label: Marx studied Smith's political economy intensively, developing Smith's labor theory while critiquing capitalist exploitation and class antagonism
description: Karl Marx engaged in a direct critique of Adam Smith's foundational principles, rejecting core axioms in favor of a dialectically opposed framework.
dialecticalTension: Negotiating the intellectual shift from Adam Smith's perspective to Karl Marx's reconstructed system.
historicalContext: Inter-epochal reception: transmitting insights from the Enlightenment & Social Contract across history into the 19th Century Divergences.

label: Mill systematized and expanded Smith's classical economic framework, integrating competitive market dynamics with utilitarian liberalism

dialecticalTension: Negotiating the intellectual shift from Adam Smith's perspective to John Stuart Mill's reconstructed system.
historicalContext: Inter-epochal reception: transmitting insights from the Enlightenment & Social Contract across history into the 19th Century Divergences.
